---
title: "13 — Which survey predictors carry the model signal?"
output: html_notebook
---

**Measures:** how much the already-selected classifier’s 2023 Brier score deteriorates when one predictor is randomly shuffled. Uses only 2023 data for interpretation and does not modify the chosen model. Importance is not a causal effect or a measure of protected-group fairness.

## Setup

Loads the unchanged input settings, shared model functions, and the persistent run
increment. The output suffix identifies this run.

```{r setup}
# Set the project root, then load R code from the shared R Notebooks.

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Project-root discovery
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Search upward for the project marker so notebook paths do not depend on a particular
# subfolder.
find_project_root <- function(start = getwd()) {
    current <- normalizePath(start, mustWork = TRUE)
    # Walk toward the filesystem root until the project marker is found.
    repeat {
        if (file.exists(file.path(current, "FMD_Project.Rproj"))) {
            return(current)
        }
        # Move up one directory; an unchanged parent marks the filesystem root.
        parent <- dirname(current)
        if (identical(parent, current)) {
            stop("Open FMD_Project.Rproj in RStudio first")
        }
        current <- parent
    }
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Notebook execution root
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Resolve the project before loading modules; configure subsequent knitr chunks to use
# that root.
project_root <- find_project_root()
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = project_root)


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared-module loader
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Extract R chunks in source order and evaluate them in the caller environment.
# This lightweight loader does not process chunk options such as eval = FALSE.
load_module <- function(name) {
    path <- file.path(project_root, "R", paste0(name, ".Rmd"))
    text <- readLines(path, warn = FALSE)
    starts <- which(startsWith(text, "```{r"))
    ends <- which(trimws(text) == "```")
    blocks <- lapply(starts, function(start) {
        # Use the next standalone closing fence for this R chunk.
        finish <- ends[ends > start][1]
        if (is.na(finish) || finish <= start + 1L) {
            stop("Missing code or closing fence in ", path)
        }
        paste(text[(start + 1L):(finish - 1L)], collapse = "\n")
    })
    eval(parse(text = paste(blocks, collapse = "\n\n")), envir = parent.frame())
    invisible(TRUE)
}


# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Shared settings and utilities
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Load configuration before helpers, retaining the existing presentation palette module.
load_module("config")
load_module("run_manager")
load_module("helpers")
load_module("plot_palette")

# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Existing-run attachment
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Attach to an allocated run rather than incrementing the counter in this stage.
run_context <- attach_run()
cat("[RUN] Current increment:", run_context$id, "\n")
```



## Estimate held-out permutation reliance

Scores the frozen model repeatedly after changing one predictor at a time, retaining all
2023 records and the original survey weights. Runs may take several minutes, especially
in full mode.

```{r estimate-permutation}
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------
# 2023 marginal permutation reliance
# -----------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Compare original and shuffled predictions from the same frozen base classifier.
# This year was used for model selection, so the interpretation is exploratory rather
# than independent.

# Evaluate predictor contribution on 2023 ONLY, before 2025 was examined.
# Shuffling a predictor breaks its observed association with the outcome and
# correlated predictors; it estimates predictive reliance, not causation.
validation <- load_run_rds("checkpoints", "02_selection_2023")
selected <- load_run_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")
fitted <- load_run_rds("models", paste0("05_", selected$chosen_family))

# The same frozen model and same survey weights are used in every comparison.
reference_prediction <- predict_classifier(fitted, validation)
reference_brier <- weighted_metrics(
    validation$FMD, reference_prediction, validation$RAW_WEIGHT
)$brier
permutation_rows <- list()
row_number <- 0L

# Set the random seed before stochastic operations so the same inputs can reproduce this
# sampling sequence.
set.seed(seed + 1305L)

# Iterate through the configured analysis items in the original execution order.
for (feature in feature_names) {
    for (replicate in seq_len(permutation_replicates)) {
        shuffled <- data.table::copy(validation)
        data.table::set(
            shuffled,
            j = feature,
            value = sample(shuffled[[feature]], size = nrow(shuffled), replace = FALSE)
        )
        shuffled_prediction <- predict_classifier(fitted, shuffled)
        shuffled_brier <- weighted_metrics(
            shuffled$FMD, shuffled_prediction, shuffled$RAW_WEIGHT
        )$brier
        row_number <- row_number + 1L
        permutation_rows[[row_number]] <- data.frame(
            feature = feature,
            replicate = replicate,
            reference_brier = reference_brier,
            permuted_brier = shuffled_brier,
            brier_increase = shuffled_brier - reference_brier
        )
        rm(shuffled, shuffled_prediction)
    }
}
permutations <- data.table::rbindlist(permutation_rows)
importance <- permutations[, .(
    mean_brier_increase = mean(brier_increase),
    min_brier_increase = min(brier_increase),
    max_brier_increase = max(brier_increase)
), by = feature][order(-mean_brier_increase)]

# Save this result under the attached run ID so it remains linked to the current
# analysis.
save_table(permutations, "13_2023_predictor_permutation_replicates")
save_table(importance, "13_2023_predictor_importance")
print(importance)
cat("Interpretation: 2023 weighted Brier degradation after independent predictor shuffling.\n")
```


## Visualize predictor reliance

Shows how much each predictor mattered to the frozen model’s probability accuracy in
2023. This is an exploratory insight, not a ranking of causal determinants.

```{r display-permutation}

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Visualize 2023 permutation-based predictor reliance
# ------------------------------------------------------------

# Express Brier deterioration relative to the original
# model's Brier score for easier interpretation.
#
# Example: A 10% increase means that shuffling the
# predictor made the Brier score 10% larger.
#
# Permutation ranges describe variability across random
# shuffles, NOT sampling-based confidence intervals.

permutation_plot_data <- data.table::copy(permutations)

stopifnot(
    all(is.finite(permutation_plot_data$reference_brier)),
    all(permutation_plot_data$reference_brier > 0),
    all(is.finite(permutation_plot_data$brier_increase))
)

permutation_plot_data[
    ,
    relative_increase_pct :=
        100 * brier_increase / reference_brier
]

# Summarize average reliance and the observed range
# across repeated random permutations.
plot_importance <- permutation_plot_data[
    ,
    .(
        mean_pct = mean(relative_increase_pct),
        min_pct = min(relative_increase_pct),
        max_pct = max(relative_increase_pct),
        repetitions = .N
    ),
    by = feature
]

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Improve predictor labels
# ------------------------------------------------------------

feature_labels <- c(
    "physical_days_group" = "Physically unhealthy days",
    "AGE_BAND" = "Age",
    "general_health_group" = "Self-rated general health",
    "SEX_CLEAN" = "Gender",
    "EDU_CLEAN" = "Education",
    "INCOME_BAND" = "Household income"
)

plot_importance[
    ,
    label := unname(feature_labels[feature])
]

# Preserve the original name for any unrecognized feature.
plot_importance[
    is.na(label),
    label := feature
]

# Rank from least to most important, so the largest
# value appears at the top of the horizontal plot.
data.table::setorder(plot_importance, mean_pct)

plot_importance[
    ,
    label := factor(label, levels = label)
]

# Make room for labels beyond the interval endpoints.
label_offset <- max(
    0.15,
    max(abs(plot_importance$max_pct)) * 0.03
)

# ------------------------------------------------------------
# Publication-style predictor importance figure
# ------------------------------------------------------------

plot <- ggplot2::ggplot(
    plot_importance,
    ggplot2::aes(y = label)
) +
    # No change in model error.
    ggplot2::geom_vline(
        xintercept = 0,
        linetype = "dashed",
        color = atg_palette[["mauve"]],
        linewidth = 0.7
    ) +
    # Range observed across random permutations.
    ggplot2::geom_segment(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = min_pct,
            xend = max_pct,
            yend = label
        ),
        color = atg_palette[["sand"]],
        linewidth = 2.5
    ) +
    # Average increase in Brier error.
    ggplot2::geom_point(
        ggplot2::aes(x = mean_pct),
        color = atg_palette[["evergreen"]],
        size = 4
    ) +
    # Directly label the average percentage increase.
    ggplot2::geom_text(
        ggplot2::aes(
            x = pmax(mean_pct, max_pct) + label_offset,
            label = sprintf("%+.1f%%", mean_pct)
        ),
        hjust = 0,
        size = 4,
        color = atg_palette[["evergreen"]]
    ) +
    ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(
        labels = function(x) sprintf("%.0f%%", x),
        expand = ggplot2::expansion(
            mult = c(0.05, 0.20)
        )
    ) +
    atg_theme() +
    ggplot2::theme(
        legend.position = "none",
        panel.grid.major.y = ggplot2::element_blank(),
        plot.caption = ggplot2::element_text(
            size = 9,
            hjust = 0,
            margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 12)
        )
    ) +
    ggplot2::labs(
        title = "Which predictors does the FMD model rely on most?",
        subtitle = paste(
            "2023 permutation reliance | Frozen",
            selected$chosen_family,
            "model"
        ),
        x = "Increase in weighted Brier score after shuffling",
        y = "Survey predictor",
        caption = paste(
            "Points show average percentage increase in Brier error.",
            "Whiskers show the range across random shuffles, not confidence intervals.",
            "\n2023 was used for model selection.",
            "Permutation reliance does not establish causation."
        )
    )

show_and_save(
    plot,
    "13_2023_permutation_importance_refined",
    11,
    5.5
)

print(plot_importance)
```
